source.summary: GitHub Actions ‘Embedder footprint’ runs for PR #349 (branch fix/335-handle-validation at head 9ec422c993f7b2e292cbedba720e6328be600628 — the #335 change (canonical handle operations validate handle indices against the instance table) with the Codex-review follow-ups (host-provided handles pass through on a local-index collision, two synthetic import-path identities of one provider resource are not distinguished at the boundary, host-supplied public-call arguments are registered at the call boundary, and a resource.drop naming a host handle wins over a colliding local entry), merged with current main b20ed79513bbb12f6e4447158fd4028808ac129b (PRs #350 and #353); ubuntu-24.04, Rust 1.96.0): workflow_dispatch runs 45604539314 and 45604546843 against the branch and pull-request run 45603104312, which built the same tree, produced byte-identical sizes for every gated series
source.derivation: Re-baseline for PR #349 (#335, canonical handle operations validate handle indices against the instance table; fourth re-baseline for this PR, after the second Codex-review follow-up commit 9ec422c — the public call boundary registers host-supplied argument handles (own arguments as host-provided handles, borrow arguments for the duration of the call), and canon resource.drop falls back to the host-provided path when the index names a host handle colliding with an unrelated local entry). Attribution was isolated by measuring current main alone three times (workflow_dispatch runs 45604554539, 45604561643 and 45604568688 on main at b20ed79513bbb12f6e4447158fd4028808ac129b; all three runs pass the gate against main's checked-in baseline, and the main control is byte-identical to that baseline on all 32 gated series). This PR's own delta against the main control is confined to the series of the three configurations that link telomere-component: in release, stripped file +9,760 B in each of component, wasi and wasi-threads and stripped .text +8,160 B (component) / +8,176 B (wasi, wasi-threads); in release-size, stripped file +6,000 B (component) / +6,016 B (wasi, wasi-threads) and stripped .text +4,560 B in each. Every other configuration is byte-identical to main in both profiles. All twelve series exceed the checked-in baseline and are re-baselined to the branch measurements; every other baseline is unchanged. Run-to-run spread was 0 B for every gated series across the three branch samples and across the three main samples. Against the original #164 baseline, the largest cumulative growth is the release component stripped file series at +11.42% (2,433,656 B to 2,711,616 B). The core-aot configuration, added by PR #267 after the #164 baseline, is not part of the cumulative comparison.
